checks.title:
我是IT服务台负责人，需要一个公司内部报修系统。员工提交问题、紧急程度和截图，服务台分派给工程师，工程师记录处理过程和解决办法，员工确认解决后关闭；仍未解决可以退回继续处理。

员工只看自己的工单，工程师只处理分派给自己的工单，服务台查看全部。新分派和处理结果及时通知相关人员，点击通知可以进入对应工单；超过24小时未解决时提醒服务台。首页展示待分派、超时工单和各工程师的工作量。

actions: 管理员创建 tickets-requester、tickets-maintainer、tickets-admin 测试账号，分别登录并完整重新加载业务页面。
员工 QA Employee 提交工单：标题、描述、Priority=High、截图 sample.png，生成 TKT-MVHFGLEH-9DEA26，附件 sample.png（99 B）可见。
服务台 QA Desk 登录后看到全部工单，将 VPN 工单分派给 QA Engineer，状态变为 In progress；另将 QA Desk 提交的打印机工单分派给 QA Engineer Two。
工程师 QA Engineer 登录后列表仅出现分派给自己的 VPN 工单；直接打开他人打印机工单 URL 显示“This ticket does not exist or you cannot see it.”；在工单中回复处理过程并附 sample.pdf，再回复解决办法并 Resolve。
员工收到分派、处理结果、已解决通知；从通知详情标题链接进入对应工单；员工执行 Reopen 退回，工单回到 In progress；工程师再次回复并 Resolve；员工执行 Confirm resolution，工单变为 Closed。
服务台首页核对 Active tickets、Unassigned、Overdue、Engineer workload 与 Recent tickets；工程师/员工首页核对各自可见工单范围。
员工尝试上传 corrupt.png 和 unsupported.exe 作为截图/附件，并提交含 unsupported.exe 的工单；服务台打开分派下拉核对候选工程师。
evidence: 正常流程可完成：员工建单（High、sample.png）、服务台分派、工程师回复处理过程+解决办法并 Resolve、员工 Reopen 退回、工程师二次处理、员工 Confirm resolution 关闭，状态依次为 Open→In progress→Awaiting confirmation→In progress→Awaiting confirmation→Closed。
角色隔离有效：员工列表仅见自己的工单；工程师列表仅见分派给自己的工单，直接打开他人工单 URL 被拒绝；服务台列表可见全部 3 张工单。
通知有效：工程师收到分派/退回通知，员工收到处理结果/已解决通知，服务台收到新工单/关闭通知；通知详情中的标题链接可进入对应工单（点击通知条目本身先打开通知详情）。
首页统计有效：服务台首页显示待分派、超时区块、工程师工作量（QA Engineer 1 active、QA Engineer Two 1 active）并随操作变化；员工首页显示自己的待确认工单。
附件校验缺陷：corrupt.png 与 unsupported.exe 均被 Screenshot/附件控件接受且无任何错误提示；unsupported.exe 还成功创建工单 TKT-MVHFOOL0-A17ECE 并作为附件展示，corrupt.png 也可追加到该工单。与清单预期的“明确失败/不支持格式反馈”不符。
超时提醒未能在本轮触发：页面存在 Overdue/Past the 24-hour target 区块和工单 24-hour target 字段，但无法在单次会话内等待 24 小时，未观察到超时提醒通知。
旁证：工程师首页仍使用报修人视角文案（Follow your requests / My open requests），并把他人提交、分派给自己的工单列在“My open requests”下；分派候选人下拉包含非工程师账号 QA Desk。

rawRetro.summary: Repaired the service-desk workflow end to end and the follow-up lint regression: the service desk can assign named engineers, engineers are limited to assigned tickets, requesters alone confirm close or reopen, assignment/handling notices reach the in-app inbox, active tickets expose a 24-hour overdue state and service-desk reminders, Home is a role-aware queue/workload dashboard, New ticket accepts a screenshot, and fresh installations with APP_SAMPLE_DATA=true receive reproducible demo accounts and tickets. Follow-up repair exposed the inbox in the sidebar instead of a header button, so the shell no longer mounts React Query hooks outside the query provider. This round repaired the realtime entry path: the application now states its WebSocket endpoint instead of deriving it from the API URL, and the session-preparation boundary releases when a socket for the current session opens after the preparation timeout, so a missed open notification can no longer leave a working application behind an "Unable to connect" screen that Retry cannot clear. This round also proved the earlier "Unable to connect" report: the verification browser's domain containment replaces WebSocket with a wrapper that drops its static readyState constants, which made the realtime client believe it was connected and never dial; the client now restores those constants before startup.

issues.title: Service desk could only assign a ticket to itself
issues.symptom: The detail action was "Accept and assign to me" with no engineer picker, and tickets-admin had no Assign grant.
issues.rootCause: The original transition modelled acceptance as self-assignment and the permission sets only granted accept/resolve/close.
issues.resolution: Added a dedicated assign transition and POST /tickets/:ticketId/assign, an engineer list endpoint, an engineer Select in the detail dialog, and an assign grant for tickets-admin. Assignment validates that the target holds tickets-maintainer or tickets-admin.

issues.title: Engineers could see and handle every ticket
issues.symptom: tickets-maintainer had Tickets: All Records and could open or resolve tickets assigned to others.
issues.rootCause: The seed granted All Records to maintainers and no assigned-only repository scopes existed.
issues.resolution: Added support.assignedTickets, support.assignedComments and support.assignedScreenshots scopes keyed on assigneeId = principal.id, changed the maintainer grants to those scopes, and added integration coverage for list isolation, detail 404 and denied assign/close.

issues.title: Requesters had no confirm-close/reopen action and staff could close early
issues.symptom: A resolved ticket offered no requester confirmation, while engineers had Close and could close before the requester confirmed.
issues.rootCause: Close was granted to service staff and the client exposed it as a normal staff transition; no reopen action existed.
issues.resolution: Moved close and reopen to tickets-requester only, exposed them through viewer booleans, added requester close/reopen UI and a reopen endpoint, and kept resolved displayed as Awaiting confirmation.

issues.title: No notification entry or assignment/handling notices
issues.symptom: The header had no bell or inbox entry and no notifications were sent for creation, assignment, replies, resolution, close or reopen.
issues.rootCause: The notification default had no channel and the ticket service had no notifier integration.
issues.resolution: Added a TicketNotifier with idempotent in-app messages targeting /tickets/:id, enabled the in-app inbox channel by default, wired best-effort sends into each transition, and gave /inbox a sidebar Notifications entry. The header stays free of an Inbox button, matching the shell contract.

issues.title: No overdue marker or 24-hour service-desk reminder
issues.symptom: Tickets had no SLA/overdue state and the service desk received no reminder for unresolved work older than 24 hours.
issues.rootCause: The ticket model only exposed status timestamps, and no periodic reminder path existed.
issues.resolution: Added overdue and slaDeadline to ticket views, an overdue badge in lists/detail/Home, and a daily-idempotent reminder sent by a 15-minute lifecycle check plus the dashboard-triggered check.

issues.title: Home remained the NocoBase demo page
issues.symptom: Every role saw Describe it/Built-in capabilities instead of unassigned, overdue, awaiting-confirmation and workload information.
issues.rootCause: The template Home component and its CAPABILITIES demo assets were still registered.
issues.resolution: Replaced Home with a role-aware dashboard using GET /api/tickets/dashboard: service staff see unassigned, overdue and engineer workload queues; requesters see their open/awaiting tickets. Removed the demo assets and rewrote the Home tests.

issues.title: New ticket form had no screenshot field
issues.symptom: A screenshot could only be attached after creating the ticket on the detail page.
issues.rootCause: The create form only submitted title, description, priority and category.
issues.resolution: Added an optional file picker to New ticket, created the ticket first, uploaded the selected screenshot through the existing attachment endpoint, and kept the ticket with a failure toast if the upload failed.

issues.title: The requested sample data was missing
issues.symptom: A fresh installation contained permission sets but no demonstrative users or tickets.
issues.rootCause: No sample seed or sampleDataToken registration existed for the application.
issues.resolution: Registered support/service-desk-demo on sampleDataToken. It creates five demo accounts (requesters, engineers and service desk), assigns their permission sets, and adds six idempotent tickets covering unassigned, overdue, in-progress, awaiting-confirmation and closed states, plus internal/public comments. It only builds on a fresh APP_SAMPLE_DATA=true installation and never overwrites existing rows.

issues.title: Service transition exhausted the connection pool
issues.symptom: Assign/accept returned 500 after a long wait with Connection pool exhausted within transaction.
issues.rootCause: The permission lookup opened database.connection() while the transition already held a transaction connection.
issues.resolution: Passed the active DatabaseConnection into userIdsWithPermission so the assign validation uses the caller's transaction.

issues.title: Overdue reminder inbox assertion raced notification delivery
issues.symptom: The integration test sometimes saw no Overdue ticket message immediately after the dashboard request even though remindOverdue sent it.
issues.rootCause: The notification manager persists the message and dispatches delivery asynchronously; the inbox was queried once with no wait.
issues.resolution: Polled the real inbox endpoint briefly until the overdue message appeared, while still asserting its title and ticket target.

issues.title: Browser harness reported Unable to connect
issues.symptom: The QA browser stalled on realtime connection before reaching business pages.
issues.rootCause: The harness WebSocket guard lost the WebSocket.CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED static constants; this is not an application defect.
issues.resolution: Recorded as a harness issue. No application change was made; QA verified the workflow after injecting the missing constants.

issues.title: Lint failed on synchronous setState inside the engineer-loading effect
issues.symptom: eslint reported react-hooks/set-state-in-effect error plus two set-state-in-effect warnings at client/pages/tickets/detail/index.tsx:197 for setEngineersLoading(true) and setAssignError(undefined) in the assign-dialog effect.
issues.rootCause: The engineer list was loaded in an effect keyed on assignOpen and set loading/error state synchronously in the effect body, causing cascading renders; fetching is actually triggered by the user opening the assign dialog.
issues.resolution: Moved the engineers request into an openAssign click handler that opens the dialog and, when the list is not cached or already loading, sets loading/error and fetches; the render path still derives loading from state. Removed the effect while keeping the ticket-detail fetch effect.

issues.title: Header InboxButton crashed the shell without a QueryClient
issues.symptom: client-shell and layout-i18n tests rendered an empty body; InboxButton threw "No QueryClient set" from the inbox hooks, and the shell navigation and page content never appeared.
issues.rootCause: The ticket feature added an InboxButton to HeaderActions that called useInboxUnreadCount/useInboxRefresh. Those hooks require the Refine QueryClientProvider and the plugin API services, neither of which the shell test harness mounts; the shell contract also says the header carries no Inbox entry.
issues.resolution: Removed InboxButton from HeaderActions, deleted the component, and exposed /inbox through a localized sidebar navigation entry (navigation.inbox). Updated the home hint and the application route test to assert the sidebar entry; shell tests render again without a QueryClient.

issues.title: Fresh browser session blocked on "Unable to connect" while the server accepted WebSockets
issues.symptom: After signing in from a completely fresh browser session, and again after a reload, the page stayed on "Unable to connect / The realtime connection could not be prepared. Retry to enter the application, or sign out." Pressing Retry repeatedly did not help, yet opening a WebSocket directly from the same page received a subscribed response, so the server-side realtime endpoint was reachable.
issues.rootCause: Not reproduced in about 44 scripted rounds at the time; it was later reproduced exactly and traced to agent-browser domain containment stripping the WebSocket static readyState constants (see the record below). The two client-side fragilities below are real but were hardening, not this failure. Two client-side fragilities match the evidence and were fixed. (1) The socket URL was derived from the API base URL as `${baseURL}/../ws`, i.e. `<basePath>/api/../ws`; it only reaches the real endpoint because `..` is collapsed, so any proxy, CDN or mount shape that keeps the segment yields a handshake the server answers as a plain 404. (2) The authentication provider owns the handshake, unsubscribes its open listener when its 10s timeout fires, and Retry only re-runs the same reconnect, so an open that arrives after the timeout (for example a transient handshake failure followed by the client's own backoff reconnect) left the failure screen permanently even though the transport was up.
issues.resolution: Client config now states api.realtimeURL = resolveAppUrl('/ws') next to api.baseURL, so the dialled endpoint no longer depends on URL normalization. SessionPreparation additionally tracks opens per session id and renders the application when a socket opened for the current session after the provider gave up; the barrier itself is unchanged (an open from the previous identity never releases it, no degraded mode, no automatic retry loop). Covered by tests/logic/session-preparation.test.tsx ('enters the application when the transport opens after the preparation timeout'), tests/logic/client-runtime.test.ts (explicit realtime URL) and the updated client-shell harness. Verified in the rebuilt production bundle by delaying the WebSocket open to 13s: the failure screen appeared, and the shell entered at ~13.6s with no Retry click; fresh sign-in, reload, in-place sign-out/sign-in and a 20s idle-then-login run all entered with no console errors, and the tickets list still renders. The proven root cause and its fix are recorded separately below.

issues.title: Client shell harness resolved an unregistered realtime service
issues.symptom: After SessionPreparation began resolving the realtime client token, all seven client-shell tests failed with 'Unexpected service token: [object Object]' and rendered an empty body.
issues.rootCause: The test harness builds its own service map with has/resolve/resolveIfCreated and throws on unknown tokens; it registered the API, authentication and authorization clients only, so the provider's resolveIfCreated call for the realtime client threw inside the render effect.
issues.resolution: Registered a fake realtime client (inactive, no-op subscribe/close/reconnect/onOpen) in the harness service map.

issues.title: Sign-in stayed at "Unable to connect" because agent-browser domain containment dropped WebSocket readyState constants
issues.symptom: Sign-in returned 200 and the session was valid, but the page remained at "Preparing your session…" and then "Unable to connect / The realtime connection could not be prepared. Retry to enter the application, or sign out." Retry and Sign out did nothing, reloading reproduced it, and no business page resources were requested.
issues.rootCause: The factory acceptance script exports AGENT_BROWSER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=127.0.0.1, and agent-browser containment then replaces window.WebSocket with a forwarding wrapper that keeps the prototype readyState values but drops the constructor static CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED. @nocobase/realtime compares `socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN`; with no socket yet and the static missing, that is undefined === undefined, so connect() returns believing a socket is already connecting and `connected` reports true while offline. The authentication provider reconnect() therefore never creates a socket, the 10s preparation gate times out, and Retry repeats the same no-op. Reproduced exactly with that environment against the factory verification server: no socket was constructed by the application, while new WebSocket(url) from the same page connected.
issues.resolution: Added client/lib/web-socket.ts restoreWebSocketReadyStateConstants() and call it in client/index.tsx before the application starts. It restores the standard 0/1/2/3 values on the existing constructor (never replacing it) and is a no-op on a native browser. Verified by rebuilding and rerunning the containment environment: WebSocket.OPEN became 1, the application dialled ws://127.0.0.1:13000/main/ws, sent both authorization subscriptions (observed with CDP Network.webSocketCreated and webSocketFrameSent), and Home plus /api/tickets/dashboard loaded. Added tests/logic/web-socket.test.ts: a wrapper without statics, a native-shaped constructor, a missing WebSocket, and an integration case that shows the real client constructs no socket until the constants are restored and then subscribes.

improvements.title: Poll durable inbox delivery in integration tests
improvements.detail: NotificationService.send persists before asynchronous channel dispatch completes. A single inbox read directly after a transition can race that dispatch.
improvements.suggestedChange: Use a bounded poll of the real inbox endpoint when asserting user-visible notifications, as the ticket workflow test now does.

improvements.title: Cover the session-preparation boundary with an open that arrives after the timeout
improvements.detail: The barrier was only tested for ready, timeout and retry. The failure mode that blocked users was an open notification delivered after the provider unsubscribed, which no test produced.
improvements.suggestedChange: When touching an authentication or realtime gate, add a case that delivers the success notification after the gate's own timeout and asserts the gate releases.

improvements.title: State derived client URLs explicitly in configuration tests
improvements.detail: api.realtimeURL was derived from api.baseURL through a `..` segment; the derivation worked only because the browser normalizes the path, so a proxy or CDN could break the handshake silently.
improvements.suggestedChange: Assert every derived-but-critical client URL (API, realtime, uploads) in a config test, and prefer stating it in client/config.

retro.summary: Repaired the service-desk workflow end to end and the follow-up lint regression: the service desk can assign named engineers, engineers are limited to assigned tickets, requesters alone confirm close or reopen, assignment/handling notices reach the in-app inbox, active tickets expose a 24-hour overdue state and service-desk reminders, Home is a role-aware queue/workload dashboard, New ticket accepts a screenshot, and fresh installations with APP_SAMPLE_DATA=true receive reproducible demo accounts and tickets. Follow-up repair exposed the inbox in the sidebar instead of a header button, so the shell no longer mounts React Query hooks outside the query provider. This round repaired the realtime entry path: the application now states its WebSocket endpoint instead of deriving it from the API URL, and the session-preparation boundary releases when a socket for the current session opens after the preparation timeout, so a missed open notification can no longer leave a working application behind an "Unable to connect" screen that Retry cannot clear. This round also proved the earlier "Unable to connect" report: the verification browser's domain containment replaces WebSocket with a wrapper that drops its static readyState constants, which made the realtime client believe it was connected and never dial; the client now restores those constants before startup.

improvements.title: Poll durable inbox delivery in integration tests
improvements.detail: NotificationService.send persists before asynchronous channel dispatch completes. A single inbox read directly after a transition can race that dispatch.
improvements.suggestedChange: Use a bounded poll of the real inbox endpoint when asserting user-visible notifications, as the ticket workflow test now does.

improvements.title: Cover the session-preparation boundary with an open that arrives after the timeout
improvements.detail: The barrier was only tested for ready, timeout and retry. The failure mode that blocked users was an open notification delivered after the provider unsubscribed, which no test produced.
improvements.suggestedChange: When touching an authentication or realtime gate, add a case that delivers the success notification after the gate's own timeout and asserts the gate releases.

improvements.title: State derived client URLs explicitly in configuration tests
improvements.detail: api.realtimeURL was derived from api.baseURL through a `..` segment; the derivation worked only because the browser normalizes the path, so a proxy or CDN could break the handshake silently.
improvements.suggestedChange: Assert every derived-but-critical client URL (API, realtime, uploads) in a config test, and prefer stating it in client/config.
